jurisdiction.name: Panama
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Panama governs AI through its National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026-2036, approved by the Cabinet Council in August 2026 and published in the Official Gazette, which builds on Executive Decree 36 of 2026 creating a national commission for critical and emerging technologies with an AI subcommission chaired by the science secretariat (SENACYT). The 2019 personal data protection law (Law 81) provides the data protection baseline. An adaptive-governance AI bill is pending in the National Assembly.
lead_institutions: Secretaría Nacional de Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación (SENACYT)
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from Official Gazette copies hosted by the National Assembly. Not yet verified from the official text: material on the national AI strategy website, the Assembly's main site and the education ministry's site. The pending AI bill, the strategy's implementation plan and planned AI governance guidelines are tracked as leads.

instruments.official_title: Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial de Panamá
instruments.english_title: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Panama
instruments.issuing_authority: Cabinet Council, on the proposal of the National Commission for Critical and Emerging Technologies and its AI Subcommission, coordinated by SENACYT
instruments.current_status: Approved by the Cabinet Council through Resolution No. 75 of 11 August 2026 ('Que aprueba la Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial de la República de Panamá'), which annexes the full strategy and takes effect on promulgation; published in Gaceta Oficial Digital No. 30592-A of 18 August 2026. The strategy was publicly launched on 30 July 2026 as part of the Agenda Nacional de Tecnologías Avanzadas. It runs from 2026 to 2036 ('IA 2036') with three-yearly reviews; an implementation plan was being prepared by the AI Subcommission in September 2026. SENACYT's 12 August 2026 news page cites the resolution as 'No. 89-26', but the gazette numbers it 75; the gazette value is recorded.
instruments.summary: Panama's first national AI strategy, valid 2026-2036 with three-yearly reviews, with the vision of making Panama a 'trusted AI innovation hub for Latin America'. It is organised in six pillars: digital and physical infrastructure; human capital; data, security and protection (built on Law 81 of 2019); governance and ethics; investment, entrepreneurship and international partnerships; and AI application in strategic economic sectors. The governance pillar rejects restrictive AI regulation in favour of sectoral regulatory sandboxes, proposes National AI Governance Guidelines, ethical impact assessments and human oversight for AI systems with significant social impact, a National Institute of Applied AI (INIAA) and an AI Risk Observatory attached to SENACYT.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Cabinet-approved national AI strategy; sets the governance architecture and the pro-innovation, sandbox-based regulatory approach for AI in Panama.

instruments.official_title: Decreto Ejecutivo N° 36 de 7 de mayo de 2026, que declara las tecnologías críticas y emergentes como áreas prioritarias y estratégicas para la República de Panamá y dicta otras disposiciones
instruments.english_title: Executive Decree No. 36 of 7 May 2026 declaring critical and emerging technologies priority and strategic areas for the Republic of Panama and issuing other provisions
instruments.issuing_authority: Executive (President of the Republic and Ministry of the Presidency)
instruments.current_status: In force: article 17 provides that it takes effect on promulgation; published in Gaceta Oficial Digital No. 30520-A of 8 May 2026. Under it the AI Subcommission was set up and the National AI Strategy was submitted to and approved by the Cabinet Council (Resolution No. 75 of 11 August 2026).
instruments.summary: Executive decree that declares critical and emerging technologies strategic national priorities to be governed by principles including ethics, transparency and security, and creates the National Commission for Critical and Emerging Technologies, chaired by the Minister of the Presidency, with specialised subcommissions chaired by SENACYT. Chapter IV establishes the AI Subcommission (SENACYT, ministries, AIG, ASEP, ANTAI, business chambers and universities) to propose AI strategies, action plans, public policies, legislative initiatives and regulations, and article 14 requires the Commission to submit a National AI Strategy for ethical, responsible, inclusive and safe AI to the Cabinet Council. State institutions must incorporate the Commission's priorities into their annual strategic and operating plans.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding instrument of Panama's national AI governance bodies (AI Subcommission) and legal basis of the National AI Strategy.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): Gaceta Oficial Digital No. 30520-A of 8 May 2026 (Assembly-digitised copy) read with pdftotext, full decree text (17 articles); the gacetaoficial.gob.pa copy returned a bot-protection page to curl.

instruments.official_title: Ley N° 81 de 26 de marzo de 2019, sobre Protección de Datos Personales
instruments.english_title: Law No. 81 of 26 March 2019 on Personal Data Protection
instruments.current_status: In force: Article 47 provides that the law takes effect two years after promulgation, and it was promulgated in Gaceta Oficial Digital No. 28743-A of 29 March 2019, which gives 29 March 2021 (date derived from that rule, not printed in the law). Regulated by Executive Decree No. 285 of 28 May 2021; the 2026 National AI Strategy builds its data-protection pillar on this law and calls for it to be adapted.
instruments.summary: Panama's general personal data protection law, setting principles (loyalty, purpose limitation, proportionality, accuracy, security, transparency and others), data-subject rights, rules for cross-border transfers and a sanctions regime for public and private bodies that process personal data. It makes the National Authority for Transparency and Access to Information (ANTAI) the supervisory and sanctioning authority, advised by a Personal Data Protection Council. It contains no AI-specific provisions but governs the personal data used to train and run AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law that applies to AI training and use; the National AI Strategy's data pillar rests on it.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): Gaceta Oficial Digital No. 28743-A of 29 March 2019 (Assembly-digitised scanned copy); law pages (articles 1-2, 32-33, 43-47 and signature page) read as rendered page images because the scan has no text layer. Status note: Executive Decree No. 285 not read; see leads. Effective date computed from art. 47: in force two years after promulgation in the Gaceta Oficial on 2019-03-29.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Panama's official gazette (through the National Assembly's copies), the Assembly's bill records, the science and digital-government agencies, ministries and regulators were searched. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for risk and assurance, the public sector, procurement, cybersecurity, transparency, standards, sandboxes, readiness indices, sectoral rules, generative AI, drafts, international agreements or historical publications. Some official sites, including the national AI strategy website, the Assembly's main site and the education ministry, were unavailable, so the status of AI bill 588 is still to be confirmed.

Law 81 effective_date cleared at merge (art. 47 'two years after promulgation', no stated calendar date). Law 81 scanned, read as images. Bill 588 status unconfirmed. Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: Gaceta Oficial (via the Assembly's digitised gazette copies; gacetaoficial.gob.pa blocks scripted access) and Assembly bill tracking: Executive Decree 36/2026 and Law 81/2019 recorded; AI bills 588 (pending) and 413 (rejected in committee) held as leads; no enacted AI law, deepfake offence or public-sector algorithm rule found.; Government: SENACYT (strategy lead), Cabinet Council, Ministry of the Presidency, AIG (digital government agency): National AI Strategy 2026-2036 recorded; AIG site search found no AI guideline for the public sector; no earlier official AI strategy found (an aggregator's claim of a 2021 AIG strategy could not be matched to any official document).; Ministries: Education (MEDUCA site unreachable; web search found teacher AI training programmes only, no guideline), health, justice, finance, labour, security: searched, nothing AI-specific found.; Regulators: ANTAI (data protection: guides list has no AI guidance), Superintendencia de Bancos (site search: no AI rule or guidance), ASEP and cyber security (searched, nothing AI-specific found).. leads.note: Pending AI framework bill (impact-based, with transparency, human-oversight and rights obligations; reportedly merging initiatives of several deputies). SENACYT's official news page of 22 September 2026 (https://www.senacyt.gob.pa/subcomision-especializada-de-inteligencia-artificial-realiza-segunda-sesion-para-trazar-la-ruta-de-implementacion-de-la-estrategia-nacional-de-inteligencia-artificial/) still calls it 'Proyecto de Ley No. 588'; secondary reports say it passed third debate and awaits executive sanction. The Assembly's bill-tracking pages could not be opened (TLS error / HTTP 503). Re-check the Assembly tracker and the Gaceta Oficial for sanction; record as binding_law once published.
